subject: Data transfer pathway & DPA/UK Addendum — onshore cache exception request
messages:
From: Maya Harris <maya.harris@clearwavehealth.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data transfer routing question — SCCs + UK Addendum

Jordan —

Thanks for the call this morning. A couple of follow-ups from our privacy and procurement teams around international routing and the UK addendum:

- We need confirmation of the primary transfer mechanism you intend to rely on for EU -> US processing (standard SCCs, or SCCs + TIA/DTIA mapping). Our legal group has asked whether Redwood will also sign the UK IDTA / UK Addendum for UK-resident data.
- Can you share the current subprocessor roster and a short attestation that no subprocessors perform persistent cross-border caching outside of EU/UK without contractual safeguards?
- We have one technical ask: for latency-sensitive clinical workloads we may want an "onshore cache" in the US that temporarily holds tokenized payloads for 12 hours before eviction. Is that compatible with your routing safeguards and the DPA wording? If so, what controls and audit logs would you provide?

I've attached our initial TIA scope (ClearWave_TIA_Scope_v1.pdf). Procurement (procurement@clearwavehealth.com) is on copy for contract timing. Hoping to get a proposed approach from you by Monday so we can align with legal.

Thanks,
Maya Harris
Sr. Privacy Counsel | ClearWave Health
maya.harris@clearwavehealth.com

Attachment: ClearWave_TIA_Scope_v1.pdf (pdf, 310KB)

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Harris <maya.harris@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer routing question — SCCs + UK Addendum

Maya —

Appreciate the note and the TIA scope. High-level response and proposed next steps below — aiming to keep both legal and technical teams happy while minimizing operational disruption: 

1) Transfer mechanism: primary boundary will be Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for EU => US. For UK-resident data we propose executing the UK Addendum (IDTA) alongside the DPA. For specific high-sensitivity datasets you flagged in the TIA we can include DTIA mappings as a supplemental exhibit.

2) Subprocessors: attaching our current subprocessor matrix and an evidence pack (redwood_evidence_pack_20260507.zip). That contains last 12-month SOC2 summary, encryption-at-rest attestations, and our default subprocessors list. We will provide a signed attestation (short form) confirming that we do not perform persistent cross-border caching outside EU/UK unless explicitly contracted and logged.

3) Onshore cache exception: we can support a time-limited onshore cache for latency-sensitive workloads, subject to:
   - Explicit clause in the DPA/UK Addendum that limits TTL to 12 hours and defines eviction semantics
   - Purpose limitation and access controls (only the serving runtime and designated ops IDs)
   - Audit logs for cache writes/reads and automated purge events (retained for 90 days)
   - Optional encryption-at-rest with customer-controlled keys (bring-your-own-KMS) if required

If ClearWave wants this enabled, legal will need an acceptance of the cache exception (we can put this in an exhibit) and engineering needs a week to stage a temp environment and sample logs. 

Next actions I propose: 
- Legal sync: Laura (legal) to draft the DPA/UK Addendum language for the onshore cache exhibit (target: Tue 05/11).
- Evidence handoff: I'll share the subprocessor matrix and evidence pack now.
- Procurement: if procurement agrees, we can issue DocuSign envelope with DPA + UK Addendum draft and the cache exhibit for signature.

Attachments: redwood_evidence_pack_20260507.zip, redwood_subprocessor_matrix.csv

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415 555 0198

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Harris <maya.harris@clearwavehealth.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, procurement@clearwavehealth.com
Date: Fri, 08 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer routing question — DPA/UK Addendum language and evidence

Maya / team —

Thanks, Jordan. A few items from Legal & Privacy to make sure the draft covers ClearWave's requirements: 

- UK Addendum: we'll include the standard IDTA signature block and an exhibit describing the mapping for UK-resident records. Please confirm the jurisdictional scoping: are you looking to apply the UK Addendum to all UK-origin records, or only to a set of named datasets in the TIA?
- Subprocessor attestations: we'll provide a CSV with subprocessors and processing locations. We will also provide an "on-demand" attestation for any subprocessor that ClearWave requests within 7 business days.
- Onshore cache exhibit: proposed contract language must include TTL = 12 hours, crypto at rest requirement (AES-256), and requirement that cache servers reside in the US region specified by ClearWave. We will include a logging requirement: audit trail for cache write/read/purge events with timestamps and principal IDs. Logs to be retained for 90 days and made available on a 30-day cadence for review.
- Technical evidence: provide HSM/KMS attestation if customer requires customer-managed keys. Our Tech Ops team will provide a sample log extract showing purge events.

I've drafted the initial DPA + UK Addendum with an onshore cache exhibit and uploaded for review. If procurement is ready, we can send via DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/1234-ABCD

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: DPA_UK_Addendum_Draft.docx

From: Maya Harris <maya.harris@clearwavehealth.com>

Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer routing question — DPA/UK Addendum language and evidence

Laura / Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the level of detail. ClearWave is comfortable with the proposed approach in principle. Two quick asks before we route to procurement: 

1) Scope: Please make the UK Addendum apply to all UK-origin records (we want blanket coverage rather than dataset-by-dataset scoping).
2) Pricing/impact: can you confirm if the onshore cache + BYOK option changes the commercial terms materially (one-time integration vs. ongoing premium)? Procurement needs a high-level estimate so they can proceed to internal approval.

We will accept the DocuSign draft once Laura updates the Addendum scope to blanket UK coverage. Procurement will follow up on pricing within 48 hours.

—
